title: Interplay of Quasiperiodic Criticality and the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Zhangyuan Chen, Xianqi Tong, Xiaosen Yang
abstract: Quasiperiodic lattices can host critical eigenstates, whereas nonreciprocal hopping in non-Hermitian lattices can induce non-Hermitian skin effect. In this work, we investigate localization phenomena in a Hatano--Nelson model with quasiperiodically modulated hopping amplitudes, where nonreciprocity arises from unequal modulation strengths of the right and left hoppings. Using a non-unitary gauge transformation, we map the non-Hermitian system into a Hermitian quasiperiodic system and obtain an exact analytical expression for the Lyapunov exponent in the thermodynamic limit. Under periodic boundary conditions, inverse participation ratios and finite-size scaling analysis are used to identify the quasiperiodic critical regimes. The comparison shows that parameter regimes hosting quasiperiodic critical states under periodic boundary conditions can exhibit the non-Hermitian skin effect under open boundary conditions. Furthermore, the non-Hermitian skin effect associated with quasiperiodic critical regimes is also observed in representative long-range hopping models and multiband extensions. Our results provide an analytically controlled perspective on how quasiperiodicity, modulated nonreciprocity, and boundary conditions jointly shape the non-Hermitian skin effect in critical regimes.
summary: This theoretical paper explores how quasiperiodic order interacts with non-Hermiticity to govern the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect. By analyzing modulated Hatano–Nelson models, the authors show that critical states found under periodic boundary conditions can induce skin effects when open boundaries are imposed. The findings extend this understanding to complex systems like long-range and multi-band lattices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the complex interplay between quasiperiodic criticality, non-Hermiticity, and boundary conditions in condensed matter models.
main_result: It demonstrates that parameter regimes exhibiting quasiperiodic critical states under periodic boundary conditions can also manifest the Non-Hermitian Skin Effect under open boundary conditions.
method: The study employs analytical techniques like non-unitary gauge transformations to map non-Hermitian systems to Hermitian ones, alongside numerical diagnostics such as Lyapunov exponents and Inverse Participation Ratios (IPR) for localization analysis.
model_or_system: The primary model is a quasiperiodically modulated Hatano–Nelson Hamiltonian. Extensions include long-range hopping terms and a two-band Rice–Mele model, all incorporating nonreciprocal hopping.
key_observables: Lyapunov exponent ($\lambda$), Directional Inverse Participation Ratio (dIPR), Mean Inverse Participation Ratio (MIPR), and the fractal dimension ($ eta$) derived from finite-size scaling.
important_parameters: The modulation strengths ($\mu_R, \mu_L$), the irrational frequency $\alpha$, and the boundary conditions (PBC vs. OBC) are crucial parameters defining different physical regimes.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping non-Hermitian systems to effective Hermitian forms via gauge transformations and analyzing the thermodynamic limit for analytical results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of MIPR/dMIPR on system size (N) to determine fractal dimensions ($ eta$) under PBC, and show schematic comparisons between nearest-neighbor, long-range, and two-band models regarding skin effect signatures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the basic quasiperiodic Hatano–Nelson model using gauge transformations and Lyapunov exponents. It then extends the analysis to include long-range hoppings and multi-band systems (Rice-Mele), consistently applying PBC/OBC diagnostics to confirm the persistence of the NHSE in critical regimes.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges concepts from topological physics (NHSE) with localization theory (quasiperiodicity), providing analytical control over how boundary conditions affect spectral properties in complex quantum systems, which has implications for photonic and cold-atom lattices.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) The dMIPR under OBC as a function of t and µR for N = 233 and θ = 0. The blue line represents the theoretical prediction from Eq. (10). The colored symbols mark the parameter points corresponding to the representa- tive eigenstates shown in (b). (b) Representative eigenstates under OBC at t = 0.5 for µR = 0.5, 1, and 2.5 from top to bottom, corresponding to the marked points in (a). (c) The analytical λ as a function of µR. The red line corresponds to t = 0.8, while the blue line represents t = 1.5.

FIG. 2. (a) The MIPR under PBC as a function of t and µR for system size N = 233 and θ = 0. The white line marks the phase transition line between the extended and critical regimes. (b) Finite-size scaling of the MIPR versus system size N on a logarithmic scale. The red points correspond to the parameter set with t = 0.3 and µR = 2.5, while the blue points correspond to t = 2.5 and µR = 2. The solid lines represent power-law fits. The statistical average is performed over 103 random realizations of the global phase θ. β is the corresponding fractal dimension.

FIG. 3. (a) Schematic illustration of the HN model with long-range hoppings. (b) The dMIPR under OBC as a function of t and µR. (c) The MIPR under PBC as a function of t and µR. Panels (b) and (c) correspond to a lattice with nearest and next-nearest neighbor hoppings, for N = 233 and θ = 0.

Figure 3(b) shows the dMIPR under OBC for a lattice with nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. The phase structure is consistent with the analytical predic- tion. For comparison, the MIPR under PBC is shown in Fig. 3(c). The PBC phase diagram retains extended and critical regimes similar to those in Fig. 2(a), indicat- ing that the long-range hopping terms do not eliminate the quasiperiodic critical eigenstate structure. Combin- ing the OBC and PBC results, we find that parameter regimes hosting critical eigenstates under PBC can also exhibit the NHSE under OBC in the long-range model.
